_comment: The runtime package payloads this release ships.
A bundle is the replaceable half of an installation, and a host's
runtime package (the compiled plugin a host loads) is release-scoped:
it must roll back with the release. So the bundle carries it.
This file is DATA, not code. The staging code iterates over whatever
is declared here and names no adapter itself, so adding an adapter is
a data change rather than a code change — and the root installer stays
host-agnostic, which is a boundary the repository enforces.
adapter    the directory under agent_installation/ that owns the
package's source
plugin_id  the id the package is registered under
validator  the stage_runtime_package.sh validator that proves the
staged package is loadable (a missing payload must fail
the promotion, not warn)
files      the EXPLICIT allowlist of files the package contains
The allowlist must agree with the adapter's own manifest
(OPENCODE_RUNTIME_MANIFEST in agent_installation/mpm-opencode/install.sh).
scripts/tests/test_runtime_bundle.py fails if the two drift apart: a
payload the adapter installs but the bundle omits is a bundle that
registers a plugin which loads NOTHING.
